PullRequest.Title: ci: Cache Electron downloads for PR tests
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Reduce repeated Electron ZIP downloads and exposure to GitHub Releases outages, such as the [HTTP 504 failures in this run](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34856241990/job/104016538390?pr=334878).

- Add one `setup-electron` action for restoring archives and preparing Electron, with `lookup-only` and opt-in `save-cache` inputs.
- Warm caches in the existing Linux, macOS, and Windows dependency jobs on `main`; restore them in PR test jobs without saving.
- Key caches by OS, target architecture, and the Electron configuration/checksums, independently of ordinary dependency changes.
- Preserve checksum validation, three-attempt retries, and the lookup-only dependency fast path when Electron is already cached.

## Validation

- Workflow and action-step expressions passed `actionlint`, allowing the existing private runner labels.
- Local checks covered cache paths, Bash/PowerShell retry behavior, 72 action-condition combinations, and 27 cache-warming combinations.
- YAML parsing and `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit hook passed; repository hygiene excludes these `.github` files and reported zero eligible files.
- Application compilation was not run: changes are limited to workflow YAML and documentation. Live cache restore/save validation remains pending CI.

## Notes

This caches the original archives, not the prepared application. Setup still validates and prepares Electron from the current checkout. The downloader still fetches `SHASUMS256.txt`, so cache hits avoid the large ZIP downloads but are not entirely network-independent. Shared caches will populate once the updated warming workflow runs on `main`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Pull-request Electron and remote test jobs on Linux, macOS, and Windows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After dependency restore and transpilation, Setup Electron must finish before Electron/remote tests run. On a warm Electron cache, the cache archive restore and Electron preparation are both on this critical path; on a cold cache, the lookup, direct download, and preparation are on it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query and, on an exact hit, download the platform Electron archive cache via actions/cache/restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One restore operation per Electron-using reusable-workflow invocation: four jobs per OS (Electron unit, Electron integration, Electron smoke, and remote), for 12 concurrent PR jobs in the current pr.yml topology. There is no cross-job coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Each relevant job invoked npm run electron directly, with no GitHub Actions cache lookup or restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each relevant job waits for its cache lookup/restore before npm run electron; a hit replaces the large GitHub Releases ZIP transfer with a cache-service transfer.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke npm run electron, which runs build/lib/electron.ts and prepares .build/electron; retry up to three times after failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful invocation per relevant job, up to three attempts on failure; unchanged effective cardinality from the deleted workflow-local retry loops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The three platform workflows each contained equivalent npm run electron retry loops at the same point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Electron preparation must complete before tests; the subprocess remains on the same workflow position as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch checksum metadata and obtain the platform Electron ZIP through @vscode/gulp-electron/@electron/get; the ZIP comes from the restored local archive on a warm cache and GitHub Releases on a miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One platform/architecture Electron setup per relevant job, with retries only after failures. Warm exact-key hits avoid the direct ZIP fetch; misses still perform it after one cache lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every clean PR runner fetched the Electron ZIP directly from GitHub Releases and then prepared .build/electron; checksum validation was already enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing Electron download/preparation remains blocking, but warm runs avoid the repeated large Releases download. Cold runs add only the cache lookup before the previous path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Remove and reconstruct .build/electron by unpacking the Electron archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per relevant job after a successful setup invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: npm run electron already removed and rebuilt .build/electron from the downloaded archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unpacking remains required and blocking; caching archives does not add another prepared-application extraction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fixed PR matrix currently has four Electron-consuming jobs per OS, so cache restores and setup execute 12 times per PR; retries scale only with failed attempts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The 12 reusable workflow jobs can run independently in parallel; within each job, cache restore and npm preparation are serialized. The diff does not add an aggregate limiter, but it replaces the prior parallel Releases ZIP downloads with cache restores on warm keys.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The exact key includes runner OS, target architecture, .npmrc, and the Electron checksum file. Main populates the cache; PRs restore without saving. Warm hits restore the original archive and still validate/prepare Electron. Cold misses perform the previous direct download after the added lookup. There are no fallback keys or negative-cache retention.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the workflow callers, conditions, cache action, retry loop, and downloader/preparation implementation are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact archive size and cache-service versus Releases throughput are not recorded in the repository; cold-cache lookup latency is also unmeasured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Warm runs substitute a cache transfer for the pre-existing large direct ZIP transfer while preserving one preparation per job; cold runs add one bounded lookup before the old path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Main-branch Linux, macOS, and Windows dependency-cache warming jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each platform job now checks the Electron cache before deciding whether node_modules only needs a lookup. On an Electron miss, dependency restoration/installation, Electron setup, and cache save must finish before that warming job completes; on a hit, only lookup operations remain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Perform an exact-key lookup-only Electron cache query.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three cache queries per main push, one in each platform job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These jobs did not query or warm an Electron archive cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lookup is on each platform job's critical path and determines whether Electron warming work is needed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore the node_modules cache archive instead of lookup-only when the Electron cache is missing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one node_modules archive restore per OS for an Electron-key miss; on an Electron hit the prior lookup-only behavior remains. A node_modules miss instead triggers the existing npm installation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All three platform cache-warming jobs passed lookup-only true, so node_modules archives were never downloaded or extracted merely to warm Electron.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The archive download and extraction are blocking only on Electron cache misses because node_modules is required to run the Electron setup script.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Setup Electron, invoking npm run electron and preparing the application on an Electron cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one successful invocation per OS and Electron cache key, with up to three attempts on failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Main dependency-cache jobs did not invoke npm run electron.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks completion of the platform warming job on a miss.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recheck the exact Electron key, download on a race hit, or upload the populated archive cache after setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One second restore/check and at most one save per OS on the initial miss path. The second check handles a cache becoming available between the lookup-only check and setup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No Electron cache restore/save boundary existed in these jobs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both operations are serialized in the miss path and the save must complete before the job ends.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch checksum metadata and download one OS/architecture Electron ZIP on a true cold cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful platform download per OS/cache key, retried up to three times on failures.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This workflow did no Electron network download; clean PR test jobs independently performed the downloads instead.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks the one warming run for a new key, then avoids the same direct ZIP download across subsequent PR jobs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Unpack and prepare .build/electron while populating the archive cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per OS on a successful cold-key warming path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Main dependency-cache jobs did not prepare .build/electron.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocking work in the cache-warming job, though only the original download archive is saved.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A fixed three-platform matrix per main push. Heavy work occurs once per OS for each new exact key, normally when Electron configuration/checksums change; warm ordinary pushes perform three lookup-only queries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Linux, macOS, and Windows warming jobs run independently and may perform up to three cold downloads/uploads concurrently; each job serializes dependency availability, Electron setup, and save.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: An exact OS/architecture/configuration key gates all heavy work. Warm hits retain the old node_modules lookup-only fast path and skip Electron setup/save. Cold misses restore or install node_modules, recheck the Electron key, download/validate/prepare Electron, and save the archive. No fallback or negative cache is used.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed conditions and all transitive cache, subprocess, filesystem, and download boundaries are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository evidence does not quantify archive size, node_modules extraction time, or main-push frequency between Electron key changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The miss path intentionally moves one bounded download/preparation per OS into main to amortize the pre-existing repeated PR downloads; warm main pushes preserve dependency lookup-only behavior apart from one small Electron cache query.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: The changed Setup Electron step is guarded by electron_tests || remote_tests, so browser-only jobs proceed from transpilation directly to browser test setup without entering the new action.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One browser-only reusable-workflow invocation per OS in the current PR matrix.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Unchanged; the three browser jobs remain independent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No Electron cache lookup, restore, download, or save runs for browser-only jobs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: workflow inputs and the unchanged guard are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material to the changed path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change for this scenario because the action is skipped.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all six changed files. Traced PR test and main cache-warming paths through cache-service network operations, node_modules restoration, npm subprocesses, direct Electron downloads, and filesystem preparation. The added work is bounded and intentionally amortizes repeated PR downloads; no high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression was found.
